episode_title: EP. 171 A Fireside Chat With the CEO of Gaine - Martin Dunn

real_qa.q: What is GAIN's core mission in the healthcare industry?
real_qa.r: GAIN's vision is to remove as much of the needless administrative waste from the healthcare industry as possible, on the basis that if they do that, those dollars flow through to care and better outcomes for patients. The company enables the interchange of information between systems that wouldn't necessarily speak to each other, allowing providers, payers, and life sciences companies to map their internal systems and transport data to other consumers.
real_qa.requete: GAIN healthcare master data management platform

real_qa.q: How much money is spent annually on updating healthcare provider databases for insurance networks?
real_qa.r: Between $2.1 and $2.3 billion a year is spent just on updating databases to get provider information current, allowing insurance companies to communicate to consumers who is in their plan, what drugs they can get on their plan, and what pharmacies they can access. With proper information flow, this spending could be cut substantially.

real_qa.q: What was Martin Dunn's first real job experience that shaped his understanding of data management problems?
real_qa.r: Martin's first real job was with an insurance company in the UK, where he was assigned to look after a big data warehouse project. This experience gave him insights into how poorly business people could explain what they needed and how poorly technology people could deliver it to them—a problem that he continues to solve today.
real_qa.requete: Martin Dunn first job insurance data warehouse

real_qa.q: Why did Delos Technology focus on pharmaceutical companies after September 11, 2001?
real_qa.r: After September 11, 2001, very few industries spent money on technology because they were uncertain about the economic future. However, life sciences and drug manufacturers like Lilly, Roche, and Bristol Myers continued to invest, remaining relatively unfazed by the slowdown. This led Delos to sell to eight of the top 10 pharmaceutical companies in the United States over the next 12 to 18 months.

real_qa.q: How many times did Martin Dunn travel between the US and South Africa to relocate his family?
real_qa.r: Martin Dunn made the US to South Africa journey more than 70 times while commuting between the two countries to relocate his family. He eventually brought his two older boys to the States and then later his two twin children, settling in San Luis Obispo on California's Central Coast.
real_qa.requete: Martin Dunn 70 times travel US South Africa

real_qa.q: What healthcare initiative does GAIN's software power in California?
real_qa.r: GAIN's software runs the Symphony Provider Directory initiative in California, which links multiple health plans and multiple provider groups. California is described as the most complex healthcare market anywhere in the world—the largest, most complex single market globally.

guest.bio_context: Martin Dunn is a serial entrepreneur spanning three continents and 25 years. He co-founded Delos Technology, which became Cyperian and is now owned by Informatica, recognized as a leading enterprise MDM platform globally. He is currently co-founder of GAIN, a next-generation master data management platform specializing in healthcare and life sciences. He has spent over 25 years as a 50-50 business partner with Jean Paquet, building multiple businesses focused on enterprise data management.
